{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABbF-57g", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhErEx8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 116, "title": "Simplify browser emulator UI and add complete responsive mobile touch controls", "body": "## Problem

The live browser emulator is functional, but its presentation is cluttered and makes the primary experience unnecessarily indirect. In current `main` (`f47caa2ef2e71c0c5361d8f3abba73d63572798b`), [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) exposes a large amount of explanatory/legal prose and a flat row of equally prominent controls. To try the bundled **潮鳴りの密室 / Shionari no Misshitsu** demo, a visitor must first click **Load demo** and *then* click **Play**. Meanwhile **Open ROM** competes visually with the primary demo action. There are no on-screen SNES controls for touchscreen-only phones.

The maintainer selected the **first, clean/light desktop concept** from the design discussion: one prominent game preview/screen, a short game title, a clear primary start action, a secondary local-ROM action and compact playback controls. The mobile concept must preserve this visual hierarchy **without sacrificing usable SNES controls**. In particular, portrait and landscape phone layouts need different positioning.

Follow the now-established [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**. This Issue is about implementing that layout and behavior, not merely adding design guidance.

## Expected outcome

A first-time visitor immediately understands **what to play and where to tap**. On desktop the bundled game is the visual focus; **one click on the prominent “Play demo / デモをはじめる” action** loads the published Shionari ROM and begins emulation without a second Play click. **Open ROM / ROMを開く** remains an obvious but secondary alternative, using the existing local-only file picker.

On smartphones the same experience is fully playable using responsive **on-screen SNES controls**, in both portrait and landscape, with the game display prioritized and the controls placed so that fingers do not unnecessarily obscure it.

Implement this as a coherent, accessible frontend change, using the existing Rust/Wasm emulator and the already bundled game. Do not substitute concept-generated artwork for an actual game screenshot or modify the game ROM to achieve the mockup.

## Layout and interaction requirements

### Desktop / large screens

- [ ] Adopt the **first light, minimal concept** as the visual direction rather than a dense dashboard: compact snes-rust header; large game preview/screen as the primary visual element; adjacent or clearly grouped game identity and **primary Play demo** action; quieter **Open ROM** secondary action.
- [ ] Keep only essential visible actions (play/pause, reset, sound/mute, optionally fullscreen/settings) and a concise state/error indication. Replace long explanatory paragraphs and the always-visible keyboard mapping with a compact **Help / Controls** or equivalent disclosure. Move the full copyright/AI-assistance/distribution notice to an accessible **About / Legal** section or link. **Do not remove** necessary licensing, local-file/privacy information, SRAM failure guidance or accessibility labels.
- [ ] Use a real game frame or a neutral placeholder before play; any promotional preview must come from a legitimate committed/derived game asset, not fabricated in-game imagery. Do not ship extra unaudited assets or unrelated games merely for decoration.

### One-action demo launch

- [ ] On a single intentional click/tap of the primary demo action, use the **same validated cartridge-loading path** as the existing `#demo` button, check the pinned Shionari ROM hash, restore its own SRAM, and **automatically start running frames** when loading succeeds. Avoid a second Play click. Reflect Loading → Playing or a clear save-recovery/error state; prevent double-starts or repeated simultaneous fetches.
- [ ] Preserve browser audio user-gesture restrictions: attempt to unlock/resume Web Audio on the *initial* activation gesture (not only after an async ROM fetch), and handle platforms that require another gesture gracefully rather than silently failing or breaking gameplay. Do not automatically play sound on initial page load without a user gesture.
- [ ] The primary action should accurately switch semantics when appropriate (e.g. Start demo before loading, Pause/Resume after activation); do not confuse **reset**, **continue** and **start again**. Selecting another ROM must preserve the existing save-before-switch and failed-save/failed-restore safeguards.
- [ ] Keep user-selected local ROMs supported and distinct from the bundled demo, including per-ROM SRAM identity. Do not upload local ROMs or SRAM.

### Smartphone portrait

- [ ] Display the game screen first at a legible size; place **touch D-pad on the left** and **A/B/X/Y on the right**, with **L/R** reachable near upper edges of the control area and **Start/Select** in a distinct lower/center position. **All twelve standard SNES buttons** (Up, Down, Left, Right, A, B, X, Y, L, R, Start, Select) must be available without opening a menu.
- [ ] Keep pause/reset, audio and other infrequent actions in a compact toolbar or overflow/settings panel. Avoid vertical pages of explanatory text while playing. Make the layout usable on narrow phones and respect safe-area insets/notches/home indicators.

### Smartphone landscape

- [ ] Provide an **actual landscape-specific play layout**, not a shrunken portrait page: center the largest practical game image; place D-pad and L on the **left** and A/B/X/Y and R on the **right**, with Start/Select easily reachable below or adjacent to the input clusters. Leave sufficient room for the game frame; do not overlay primary controls on important pixels by default.
- [ ] Adapt to short-height landscape viewports, browser toolbars and safe areas, without clipped buttons, forced horizontal scrolling, accidental browser zoom or a need to rotate back to portrait to operate Start/Select/L/R.
- [ ] Handle portrait↔landscape transitions, fullscreen entry/exit and window resizing while a game is running without resetting the core, corrupting video geometry, losing SRAM, or keeping stuck virtual buttons.

### Touch and input behavior

- [ ] Wire virtual controls through the **existing standard SNES button bitmasks**, alongside keyboard and Gamepad API. Preserve keyboard and physical gamepad support; sources may coexist without one clearing another's held buttons.
- [ ] Implement **true multi-touch** (hold direction + A/B, L/R + face button, simultaneous buttons, and D-pad diagonals as appropriate); process pointer/touch cancel, release outside the control and visibility/blur/orientation transitions to avoid stuck input. Prevent scrolling/long-press selection on the gameplay controls without breaking scrolling or keyboard focus elsewhere.
- [ ] Use comfortably sized touch targets (aim for at least ~44 CSS px where space permits), clear pressed/disabled feedback, appropriate accessible names and focus states, and no hard reliance on hover. Keep audio, input and display updates responsive on representative mobile device viewport sizes.

## Context and scope

The bundled Shionari demo was integrated in [Issue #110](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/110), updated to **candidate E with dialogue blips** by [Issue #112](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/112), and remains the sole bundled public game ROM. Do not restore the older two-step demo workflow or change the ROM, its provenance/legal notice, hash pin, CSP or the Pages artifact allowlist except as explicitly justified by the interface.

Current frontend entry points: [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [`web/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js), real browser tests in `web/tests`, and production builder `tools/build-web.mjs`.

Stay within the existing dependency-light static site, native Canvas, browser APIs and Wasm core. No large component framework or backend is required.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] **Desktop:** a newcomer sees one visually dominant demo-start action, a clearly secondary Open ROM action and a game screen; excessive always-visible explanatory text is removed but accessible Help, Legal and safety/error information remain available.
- [ ] **One-tap demo:** from a fresh load, clicking/tapping Play demo downloads the pinned same-origin ROM, restores or safely handles battery SRAM, and progresses into genuine emulated gameplay **without clicking Play again**. Check pending and failure paths, double click, repeat play/pause/reset, and local-ROM switching. Test Web Audio activation under user gesture restrictions and provide meaningful feedback when audio cannot be enabled.
- [ ] **Full touch controls:** a real browser test uses pointer/touch inputs to assert each of Up/Down/Left/Right, A/B/X/Y, L/R and Start/Select reaches the emulator as its correct SNES bit. Test diagonals and simultaneous combinations, independent keyboard/gamepad overlap, pointer cancellation and release outside/blur so no buttons stick. Prefer observable core/controller state rather than only testing CSS pressed styles.
- [ ] **Portrait and landscape:** Playwright touch-capable mobile viewports (including a narrow portrait device and a short-height landscape device) verify that the display and **all twelve buttons** are visible, hit-testable, and do not overflow or require horizontal scrolling. Test orientation/viewport resizing while running, safe-area-aware layout, rendering geometry and pausing/resuming.
- [ ] **Gameplay:** bundled Shionari can be operated from an actual mobile-oriented test with touch controls, including a visible game-state/video change. Keep original game behavior and save state; do not insert game-specific hacks.
- [ ] Preserve existing 256/512 framebuffer handling, audio scheduling/mute, SRAM isolation and failed-save/restore safety, local-file privacy, WebAssembly initialization, CSP and Pages subpath. Existing Castle/Memory fixture and original diagnostic tests remain intact.
- [ ] Run and record formatting, warning-denying Clippy, Rust workspace tests, reproducible source-built cleared-game/hardware fixtures when relevant, production Wasm build and the full mandatory Chromium/Playwright suite including Pages smoke. Update test selectors deliberately if markup changes and retain meaningful behavioral coverage; no blanket skipping.
- [ ] Include before/after screenshots of **desktop, phone portrait and phone landscape** from the actual tested UI in the PR or validation document, plus a concise description of interaction choices, device/viewport dimensions, test results and known limitations. Do not misrepresent concept images as production screenshots.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari/Android Chrome devices, Bluetooth controllers, accessibility/assistive technology checks and human usability feedback. These improve confidence but are not required before merge when browser-based checks are executable. Any platform-specific limitation observed must be documented rather than hidden.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge, the PR author/merger checks the new `main` GitHub Pages deployment and verifies the **actual published site** on a desktop and responsive mobile viewport: one-tap demo launch, visible controls in portrait/landscape, relative ROM/Wasm asset requests, and absence of 404/CSP/MIME/runtime errors. This post-merge-only confirmation is **not** a pre-merge approval condition. Record the deployment URL/run and results. On a failure, open a follow-up `task` Issue with reproduction and logs. AI agents cannot perform background monitoring unless separately invoked.
